newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US bond vols firm, looking to employment.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US bond vols firm, looking to employment.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options marched higher Monday as the focus turned to Friday's May U.S. employment report.
July rose 0.5 point to 8.8 percent from the previous session and September gained 0.1 point to 8.5 percent.
"You're getting a modest bid in front of employment. We'll probably keep vols artificially bid before the number," said a trader for a U.S. brokerage.

The market traditionally pumps up options volatility in the days before the monthly U.S. jobs report due to the data's track record of setting trends for bond prices, but that pattern has not held up in recent months.

So it is significant that the old trend has returned, and volatilities are again holding a bid before the report, said a floor broker for a European banking firm. He noted July has gained more than 1.5 points since dropping as low as 7.2 percent just over a week ago.
The average forecast for May non-farm payrolls is for a gain of 221,000, with the unemployment rate predicted to rise to 5.0 percent from 4.9 percent, according to a Reuters survey.
Options traders said the highlight of the session occurred early, when a Wall Street dealer firm sold 4,000 September 104-00 puts.

September bond futures ended 4/32 higher at 109-24 after a stronger than expected U.S. purchasing managers report trimmed robust opening gains. The National Association of Purchasing Management said its May index rose to 57.1 from April's 54.2, exceeding the average forecast of 53.9.

Traders said Wednesday could prove pivotal for the market, with Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan addressing the International Monetary Conference in Interlaken, Switzerland, and the jobs data drawing nearer.
"Wednesday will probably be a big day for Fed headlines, and probably a big volatility day," said a U.S bank trader.
In Eurodollars, the morning price break unleashed modest put buying on the way down, but interest dried up as prices traded sideways for the rest of the day, floor traders said.

Market participants are generally hesitant to sell straddles and strangles before Friday, although one large sale in the September 94.00/94.25 strangle weighed on nearby volatility, one Eurodollar broker said.
September volatility slipped about 0.2 point to 8.8 percent, with December also declining modestly to 10.8 percent.
